title: Major Shift: Supreme Court Reshapes Executive Power - NewsBreak
text: President Donald Trump is expected to increasingly push the boundaries of executive power following the latest Supreme Court rulings, according to legal expert Alan Dershowitz. Dershowitz has outlined potential responses from the Trump administration to perceived judicial overreach, including challenging individual judges’ authority. Dershowitz argued that individual judges cannot enforce broad restrictions on presidential actions. Dershowitz said, “There are two things that could happen. One, the administration could go in front of these judges and say ‘Look, withdraw your opinion. You are now in violation of the Supreme Court.’ That’s one possibility.” Dershowitz added, “That’s what I would advise. The other possibility is for the administration simply to ignore these injunctions and say they’re no longer operative.” The Supreme Court ruled on Trump’s bid to end birthright citizenship, with a 6–3 split favoring the executive order. CASA, Inc., a nonprofit organization based in Maryland that advocates for immigrant rights, argued it violated the 14th Amendment. The conservative majority sided with Trump. Dershowitz warned of escalating tension between the executive and judicial branches. He argued both branches must respect constitutional limits. Dershowitz said, “Sure, they control the particular litigants in the case, but we’re not going to be bound by them because the Supreme Court has said that single justices, judges don’t have the authority to bind the administration.” Dershowitz added, “Look, we live at a time when there is a battle between the judiciary and the executive. President Trump has pushed the envelope further than any president since Franklin Delano Roosevelt.” Dershowitz stated, “So it’s not surprising the Democrats would respond by pushing the envelope. But, as Justice Amy Coney Barrett said, just because you think the executive has exceeded their constitutional power doesn’t mean the judiciary should exceed its judicial power. Both branches of government have to remain within their constitutional constraints.” Sarah Bennett covers U.S. politics & news for content partner Modern Newsstand LLC.
